items.front: When and how was the Planning Commission set up, and its status?
items.back: 1950, by an executive resolution — a non-statutory, non-constitutional body chaired by the PM.
items.examPoint: Planning Commission — established 1950 by executive resolution, non-statutory, PM as chair

items.back: Visvesvaraya Plan 1934; NPC 1938 (Bose, chaired Nehru); Bombay Plan 1944 (Tata & Birla); People's Plan 1945 (M.N. Roy).
items.examPoint: Pre-independence planning efforts — Visvesvaraya Plan (1934), NPC (1938), Bombay Plan (1944), Gandhian & People's Plan

items.front: Growth models of the first three Five-Year Plans?
items.back: First = Harrod-Domar (saving/investment); Second = Mahalanobis (heavy industry); Third = Gadgil-Yojana.

items.front: Second Plan (1956-61) — model and signature projects?
items.back: Mahalanobis model; heavy industry & PSUs — Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur steel plants.
items.examPoint: Second Plan (1956-61) — Mahalanobis model, heavy industry & PSUs, steel plants

items.front: Why did the Third Plan (1961-66) fail, and what followed?
items.back: 1962 Indo-China & 1965 Indo-Pak wars + drought; followed by the Plan Holiday (1966-69).
items.examPoint: Third Plan (1961-66) — Gadgil Yojana, failed due to wars & drought

items.back: 1966-69: three annual plans replaced the regular Five-Year Plan after the Third Plan's failure.
items.examPoint: Plan Holidays (1966-69) — annual plans after Third Plan failure

items.front: Fifth Plan slogan and Rolling Plan period?
items.back: Fifth (1974-78) = 'Garibi Hatao' + Minimum Needs Programme; Rolling Plan = 1978-80 (Janata govt).
items.examPoint: Fifth Plan (1974-78) — Garibi Hatao & Minimum Needs Programme

items.front: Which was the last Five-Year Plan, and when did the plan era end?
items.back: Twelfth Plan (2012-17) was the last; plans gave way to NITI Aayog after 2017.
items.examPoint: Later plans (9th-12th) — inclusive growth; Twelfth (2012-17) was the last plan

items.front: When was NITI Aayog created and by what instrument?
items.back: 1 January 2015, by a Union Cabinet resolution — a policy think-tank (not a statute).
items.examPoint: NITI Aayog — established 1 Jan 2015; policy think-tank; structure (Governing Council, PM chair, Vice-Chairman, CEO)

items.front: Key difference: Planning Commission vs NITI Aayog?
items.back: PC allocated central funds (top-down); NITI has NO fund-allocation role (now Finance Commission) — cooperative federalism.
items.examPoint: Planning Commission vs NITI Aayog — NITI has no fund-allocation role (now with Finance Commission)

items.front: NITI Aayog structure (chair, council, VC, CEO in 2026)?
items.back: PM = Chairperson; Governing Council = all CMs; VC Suman K. Bery; CEO B.V.R. Subrahmanyam.
items.examPoint: NITI Aayog — established 1 Jan 2015; policy think-tank; structure (Governing Council, PM chair, Vice-Chairman, CEO)

items.back: Aspirational Districts Programme, SDG India Index, National MPI, Atal Innovation Mission.
items.examPoint: NITI Aayog initiatives — Aspirational Districts, SDG India Index, National MPI, Atal Innovation Mission

items.front: NITI's planning documents and the Viksit Bharat vision year?
items.back: 3-Year Action Agenda, 7-Year Strategy, 15-Year Vision; Viksit Bharat = developed India by 2047.
items.examPoint: NITI planning documents — 3-Year Action Agenda, 7-Year Strategy, 15-Year Vision
